title: Clustering, anomalías y validación temporal
scope: LESSONS_ONLY: title/tagline/job relevance, 8 outcomes, 44/44 theory/reference paragraphs, 9 theory code/output blocks, 9 callouts, 3 figures, plus the S36-specific interactive playground rendered inside Theory. I Do / We Do / You Do / self-check / exams excluded.

roadmap.T1: Clustering: escalamiento y k-means/density; elección, estabilidad y métricas limitadas.
roadmap.T2: Dimensión: PCA y visualización; interpretación prudente de proyecciones.
roadmap.T3: Anomalías: Isolation Forest/LOF y reglas; novelty vs outlier y contamination.
roadmap.T4: Tiempo y evaluación: backtests temporales; etiquetas escasas y utilidad de revisión.
roadmap.gate: Señales no supervisadas que ayudan al triage sin convertir rareza/cluster en conducta indebida y sin leakage temporal.

live_status.public_card_tagline: Señales auxiliares evaluadas por utilidad de revisión; una anomalía nunca es conclusión de conducta indebida.
live_status.reason: The available public crawl is approximately four weeks old; hours drift is not promoted to a current deployment defect without a fresh hydrated render.

research_basis.use: KMeans minimizes within-cluster sum-of-squares, requires k and centroids are means; cluster geometry and internal metrics have limitations.
eps is a neighborhood distance and min_samples includes the point itself; both are data/metric-dependent parameters.
Mean/std are fitted on training samples and stored for later transform; scaling is part of fitted state.
PCA centers but does not scale features automatically; components are learned directions of maximum variance and explained_variance_ratio has a specific meaning.
Outlier and novelty detection have distinct operating assumptions; LOF novelty=True must score new unseen data only.
contamination is used to determine a score threshold/proportion of outliers, not intrinsically a human-review capacity parameter.
Time-ordered splits prevent training on future data; optional gap separates train and test boundaries.
ARI compares partitions and is invariant to cluster-label permutations, suitable for actual partition-stability checks.

runtime_counterexamples.impact: empty batch has no controlled contract
zip silently drops two data rows
negative cluster label silently indexes last cluster
invalid density policy marks every point core
nonfinite internal score can become chosen k
one-sided projection check misses a large negative-side outlier
guard allows the exact moralized naming pattern prohibited by prose
default self-reference lets the outlier contaminate its own baseline
invalid contamination yields impossible negative workload
training on a future month is not detected
invalid rates outside [0,1] are averaged as valid
k larger than ranking support is silently treated as missing negatives

rejected_findings.claim: The DBSCAN core-point convention incorrectly excludes/includes the point itself.
rejected_findings.evidence: The source explicitly counts the point itself, matching current sklearn DBSCAN semantics.

rejected_findings.claim: The fixed-weight PCA toy falsely claims to implement real PCA.
rejected_findings.evidence: The source explicitly says the weights are fixed scaffolding, not learned eigenvectors, and distinguishes weight_share from explained variance.

rejected_findings.claim: The Isolation Forest fixed-cut path toy is presented as the real ensemble.
rejected_findings.evidence: The source explicitly says it is a one-path toy and not the real ensemble.

rejected_findings.claim: The section equates clustering/anomaly with guilt.
rejected_findings.evidence: The prose repeatedly rejects guilt/fraud/parentesco conclusions; defects are in executable enforcement and evaluation, not the stated ethical principle.

rejected_findings.claim: min_samples excluding the sample itself is required.
rejected_findings.evidence: sklearn includes the point itself; current text is correct.

rejected_findings.claim: Scaling before every KMeans/PCA is a universal mathematical requirement.
rejected_findings.evidence: Scaling is often appropriate when units should contribute comparably, but feature units/weights may be intentionally meaningful; the source overstates this rather than being directionally wrong.

rejected_findings.claim: 19h public versus 9h source is a confirmed current deployment bug.
rejected_findings.evidence: Public crawl is stale; requires fresh hydrated render.

findings.summary: S36 assumes S35 outputs are valid even though S35 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED.
findings.fix: Require machine-valid S35/S34 prediction, policy, explanation and audit artifacts before unsupervised signals enter the case file.

findings.summary: Cluster/anomaly/P@k artifacts lack sample IDs, dataset snapshot, feature-set, scaler, detector/run, threshold policy and as-of lineage.
findings.fix: Introduce immutable UnsupervisedSignalManifest and keyed rows.

findings.summary: misconduct_auto=False, verdict=False, human_review=True, auto_guilt=False and similar flags are literals rather than validators.
findings.fix: Validate structured action/claim semantics and human-routing state.

findings.summary: Because section.id is ai-apis-advanced, the Theory playground renders a function-calling/LLM demo instead of clustering/anomaly content.
findings.fix: Update SectionView mapping for ai-apis-advanced to an S36-specific clustering/anomaly playground while preserving stable progress ID.

findings.summary: Scaling is described as non-optional rather than a modeling/feature-weighting choice tied to metric and units.
findings.fix: Explain when standardization is appropriate and that deliberate units/weights can legitimately change geometry.

findings.summary: K-means is described as repeating until nothing moves, ignoring tolerance/max_iter stopping.
findings.fix: Say until convergence within tolerance or iteration limit.

findings.summary: A one-feature 1D standardization demo cannot demonstrate cross-feature magnitude domination, which is the scale problem being taught.
findings.fix: Use at least a 2-feature point set with deliberately different units for the scale-trap demonstration.

findings.summary: zscore_list crashes on empty input and returns scaled=True with NaN/nonfinite values.
findings.fix: Validate non-empty finite input and return a fitted scaler state only after successful validation.

findings.summary: Scaling stats are recomputed from the current batch and not persisted/versioned for later temporal scoring.
findings.fix: Fit scaler on declared reference/train data and transform later data with the frozen state.

findings.summary: update_centroids uses zip without exact cardinality checks and accepts invalid/negative labels.
findings.fix: Require len(xs)==len(labels), integer labels in [0,k), valid k and matching prev length.

findings.summary: density_core_1d accepts negative eps and nonpositive min_samples, producing meaningless masks.
findings.fix: Validate finite eps>=0 and integer min_samples>=1.

findings.summary: The rolling-origin temporal-backtest figure is attached to T1-B choice-of-k instead of T4-A temporal validation.
findings.fix: Move the figure to T4-A and give T1-B a clustering-stability visual if needed.

findings.summary: Multi-seed k selection consumes two handwritten k→score maps rather than running seeded clusterings.
findings.fix: Run repeated seeded clustering on the same frozen data and compute actual internal metrics.

findings.summary: Same chosen k across seeds is not partition stability; cluster assignments may be incompatible.
findings.fix: Compare partitions using ARI or another label-permutation-invariant measure and centroid/assignment sensitivity.

findings.summary: choose_k crashes on empty maps, accepts NaN and has implicit tie behavior.
findings.fix: Validate non-empty finite score maps and version deterministic tie policy.

findings.summary: The prose says k incorporates queue capacity/business sense, but code never consumes or tests capacity.
findings.fix: Separate geometric candidate selection from an explicit downstream segmentation/queue constraint and document why k should or should not depend on it.

findings.summary: Learners are warned not to punish cluster IDs but are not explicitly taught that numeric cluster labels are arbitrary/permutation-invariant across runs.
findings.fix: Add a concrete label-swap example and prohibit semantic reliance on cluster number.

findings.summary: silhouette and ARI appear without enough self-contained explanation for their interpretation/limits.
findings.fix: Define silhouette at intuitive point-vs-own/neighbor-cluster level and expand ARI before use.

findings.summary: scale_xy crashes on empty input, propagates nonfinite values and has no reusable fitted state while reporting scaled=True.
findings.fix: Validate input and separate fit_scale from transform_scale with manifest lineage.

findings.summary: weight_share_pc1 is coefficient-mass share, not explained variance or a robust importance measure; zero vector returns 0.0 as if meaningful.
findings.fix: Rename to coefficient_abs_share_feature0 and reject zero-mass vectors.

findings.summary: far_from_mean checks only max(pc)-mean and misses equally distant negative-side points; NaN can false-green.
findings.fix: Validate finite pc and evaluate absolute deviation or an explicitly defined distance statistic.

findings.summary: axis-name guard forbids only fraude/culpa and allows labels such as riesgo_moral or sospechoso despite prose forbidding them.
findings.fix: Use a structured allowed naming scheme rather than a two-token blacklist.

findings.summary: A far PCA projection directly produces review_queue without the frozen S34/S35 threshold/abstention policy, evidence requirements or capacity accounting.
findings.fix: Route exploratory signals through the governed decision-policy manifest; PCA alone cannot enqueue.

findings.summary: The text says IF/LOF contamination expresses review capacity; sklearn defines it as the contamination/proportion used to determine the outlier threshold.
findings.fix: Keep model score/contamination semantics separate from a downstream queue-capacity threshold policy.

findings.summary: sigma_flags detects only upper-tail values and misses low anomalies.
findings.fix: Define one-sided business rule explicitly or use absolute/two-sided deviation when teaching general anomaly detection.

findings.summary: sigma_flags defaults ref to xs despite prose requiring an explicit clean/past reference, letting anomalies contaminate their own baseline.
findings.fix: Require an explicit frozen reference manifest; remove ref=None fallback for the gate path.

findings.summary: Replacing sd=0 with 1.0 makes a 3-sigma threshold arbitrary in original units for a constant reference.
findings.fix: Handle constant-reference features explicitly: unchanged values are in-reference; deviations require a declared measurement tolerance/data-quality policy.

findings.summary: NaN/nonfinite values, invalid z thresholds and malformed references are not rejected; NaN is scored as non-anomalous.
findings.fix: Validate finite reference/score inputs and positive finite z before anomaly scoring.

findings.summary: Outcome promises knowing when IF/LOF applies, but current text omits the sklearn LOF novelty=True constraint that predict/score methods must be used on new unseen data only.
findings.fix: Add the outlier-vs-novelty API distinction and its evaluation consequence.

findings.summary: expected_flags accepts negative or >1 contamination, noninteger/negative n and can return impossible workloads.
findings.fix: Validate domain and separate sklearn estimator contamination constraints from queue-policy fractions.

findings.summary: int(n*contamination) is presented as expected flagged count even though estimator thresholds/ties and algorithm semantics need not produce that exact integer; detector parameter is conflated with policy threshold.
findings.fix: Treat this only as a queue-budget calculation on an explicitly defined policy fraction, not estimator output.

findings.summary: has_leakage only checks duplicate month and misses training months later than test month.
findings.fix: Parse real timestamps and enforce max(train_time) < min(test_time), with optional gap/availability-time rules.

findings.summary: Backtest arrays have no sample IDs, event/availability timestamps or reference snapshot, so chronology and late-arrival correctness cannot be reconstructed.
findings.fix: Use keyed time-aware rows and frozen reference manifests.

findings.summary: backtest=True is hard-coded and window flag rates are handwritten rather than derived from the scored future rows.
findings.fix: Derive windows from prediction rows and compute a machine-valid backtest result.

findings.summary: mean_flag_rate crashes empty and accepts rates outside [0,1] without support/denominators.
findings.fix: Validate non-empty windows, 0<=rate<=1 and carry counts/support per window.

findings.summary: A review click/utility proxy is said to suffice without discussing that only reviewed cases may receive labels, creating selective feedback.
findings.fix: State the feedback sampling/coverage problem and distinguish operational utility feedback from unbiased detector evaluation.

findings.summary: T4-B accepts an already-ranked binary utility list rather than sample IDs+scores, so ranking correctness and ties cannot be audited.
findings.fix: Compute top-k from keyed scores with deterministic/versioned tie policy.

findings.summary: k can exceed ranking length and labels can be nonbinary, yielding silent denominator distortion or precision >1.
findings.fix: Require 1<=k<=n and binary/validated utility labels for labeled rows.

findings.summary: human_in_loop=True/auto_guilt=False are hard-coded; n_labels/n_flags scarce condition is described but not implemented.
findings.fix: Require reviewer identity/routing/capacity and derive scarcity/coverage from actual counts.

findings.summary: If labels are generated mainly by reviewing top-ranked cases, P@k cannot by itself estimate overall detector quality and can reinforce its own selection policy.
findings.fix: Track review coverage/sampling strategy and use blinded/random audit samples where needed for evaluation.

findings.summary: 'precision@k + feedback humano > ROC inventado' is too absolute; metric choice depends on target, label coverage and operating objective.
findings.fix: Frame P@k as primary queue-utility metric for this lab, not universally superior to ROC-based evaluation.

findings.summary: Since S27 pytest is systematic, yet S36 theory gates remain prints, literals and toy outputs rather than collected regression tests.
findings.fix: Add pytest regressions for scaling, cardinality, invalid parameters, temporal leakage, contamination and P@k.

findings.summary: AML, LOF, ARI, silhouette, path length and several English process terms appear without consistent Spanish-first introductions.
findings.fix: Expand/define each on first use and then reuse the compact industry term.

highest_risk_findings: S36-F04 current Theory playground is function-calling/LLM content because the legacy ai-apis-advanced ID still routes to the old demo
S36-F08/F10/F11 preprocessing/clustering helpers accept invalid data/parameters and can certify broken state
S36-F13/F14 k stability is based on handwritten score maps and does not measure partition stability
S36-F21/F22 PCA interpretation misses negative-side outliers and moralized names despite claiming guards
S36-F24/F30/F31 contamination is conflated with review capacity and invalid fractions produce impossible workloads
S36-F25/F26/F27/F28 sigma anomaly rule is one-sided, self-contaminating by default and unsafe under zero variance/NaN
S36-F32/F33/F34 temporal backtest cannot prove no future leakage and prints backtest=True
